children: is talking to potential buyers to facilitate a secondary share sale for one of its major real estate funds, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.
Shares were 2.41% higher at $126.42 during pre-market trading.

The transaction, in which the alternative asset manager is taking a more formal role, is expected to allow some of the fund's existing investors to cash out, according to the report published on Thursday.
The news comes as a period of high interest rates weighs on returns and leads investors to seek redemptions, according to the report.
